answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped unless it is backed by a unique, nontransferable stake that is locked for a long period and slashed when independent audits find coordinated fraud. A sybil operator can still mint identities, but cannot cheaply multiply voting weight: every extra identity needs its own capital, and a linked cluster risks losing it. This turns a fable of effortless influence into an echo of costly commitments, while a prism of diverse, randomly sampled auditors makes one operator’s control harder to hide.
